policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Active ἐποίησαν and middle ἐποιήσαντο both yield ASV 'made great lamentation over him'; the English shows no voice distinction and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'the city of Samaria' supplies a definite article that English requires with or without Greek τὴν; the wording does not distinguish the readings.
ASV opens 'And the multitudes'; δὲ and τε are both carried by that connective, so the English does not distinguish them.

ASV reads 'For from many of those that had unclean spirits, they came out' — the partitive 'from many' renders the genitive Πολλῶν, not a nominative subject πολλοὶ, which is instead the margin's 'For many of those ... came forth'.
ASV 'they came out' is plural, rendering plural ἐξήρχοντο with the spirits as subject; singular ἐξήρχετο would give 'it came out'.
ASV 'And there was much joy' renders either ἐγένετο δὲ or Καὶ ἐγένετο; the connective and verb are identical in English.
ASV reads 'much joy', rendering πολλὴ χαρὰ; χαρὰ μεγάλη would give 'great joy'.
ἐξιστάνων and ἐξιστῶν are alternate present-participle forms of the same verb, both rendered 'amazed'; the English cannot distinguish them.
ASV 'to whom they all gave heed' renders πάντες explicitly; the reading that omits it leaves nothing for 'all'.
ASV 'that power of God which is called Great' renders the participle καλουμένη; without it the phrase would be simply 'the great power of God'.
ASV has 'good tidings concerning the kingdom of God' with no object noun; τὰ περὶ would require 'the things concerning', as in the reading it revises away from.
ASV 'beholding signs and great miracles wrought' keeps σημεῖα first and attaches μεγάλας to δυνάμεις, matching σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας; the other reading reverses the order and lacks 'great'.
The added article τὸν before Πέτρον has no English exponent; ASV 'they sent unto them Peter and John' is the same either way.
οὐδέπω and οὔπω are synonymous; ASV 'for as yet it was fallen upon none of them' renders either.
ASV reads 'into the name of the Lord Jesus', rendering κυρίου; χριστοῦ would give 'Christ Jesus'.
ἐπετίθεσαν and ἐπετίθουν are alternate imperfect forms of the same verb, both 'laid they their hands'.
ASV 'when Simon saw' renders ἰδὼν or Θεασάμενος equally; the mapped note concerns 'Holy', not this participle.
ASV text reads 'the Holy Spirit', requiring τὸ ἅγιον, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit Holy' places the shorter πνεῦμα in the margin.
ἔναντι and ἐνώπιον are synonymous; ASV 'is not right before God' renders either.
ASV reads 'pray the Lord', rendering κυρίου; θεοῦ would give 'God'.
ASV 'returned to Jerusalem' does not distinguish imperfect ὑπέστρεφον from aorist ὑπέστρεψαν.
Ἱεροσόλυμα and Ἱερουσαλήμ are both rendered 'Jerusalem'; the spelling has no English exponent.
ASV 'preached the gospel to many villages' does not distinguish imperfect εὐηγγελίζοντο from aorist εὐηγγελίσαντο; the mapped note is a Greek gloss on the verb's sense, not a variant.
The added article τῆς before Κανδάκης has no English exponent in 'under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians'.
ASV opens 'and he was returning'; τε and δὲ are both carried by that 'and'.
Both orders yield English 'Isaiah the prophet'; Greek word order here has no exponent in the ASV.
ASV 'except some one shall guide me' fits future indicative ὁδηγήσει and aorist subjunctive ὁδηγήσῃ alike after ἐὰν μή.
ASV 'before his shearer is dumb' renders the substantival participle without marking aorist κείραντος against present κείροντος.
ASV 'In his humiliation' supplies a possessive that the article τῇ alone licenses in English, so it does not require the added αὐτοῦ.
ASV 'His generation who shall declare?' has no connective, but δὲ is routinely left unrendered in ASV; the English does not settle its presence.
ASV 'of whom speaketh the prophet this?' renders τοῦτο; the reading that omits it leaves the demonstrative unaccounted for.
ASV ends the verse at 'what doth hinder me to be baptized?' with no verse 37, excluding the TR expansion; the remaining two readings differ only in punctuation, which the English cannot distinguish.
